sources.entry: google-webfonts-helper ⚠ - Hassle-Free Way to Self-Host Google Fonts. Get eot, ttf, svg, woff and woff2 files + CSS snippets. (Demo) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: A web service and JSON API that lets you self-host Google Fonts by generating font files (eot, ttf, svg, woff, woff2) and CSS snippets for a chosen font, style, and charset.
summary.what_it_does: The service lets you pick a Google font, its variants (styles/weights), and character subsets, then provides CSS @font-face snippets and downloadable font files in .eot, .woff, .woff2, .svg, and .ttf formats, optionally as a zip archive. Its JSON API lists all fonts sorted by popularity and returns per-font URLs to the font files on Google's servers, with optional subset, format, and variant filtering on zip downloads. It runs as an Express server, with prebuilt Docker images published via GitHub Packages. A Google Fonts API key is required via the GOOGLE_FONTS_API_KEY environment variable. The README says the API is public but rate limits may apply.
use_cases: Self-host a Google font on your own web server
Download Google font files in woff, woff2, ttf, eot, or svg formats
Generate @font-face CSS snippets for a Google font
Fetch Google font metadata and file URLs via a JSON API
Bundle a filtered set of font variants and subsets into a zip
how_to_run: Get your own Google Fonts API key (link in README) and put it in a .env file: echo "GOOGLE_FONTS_API_KEY=<key>" > .env
Development: ./docker-helper.sh --up, then inside the container: yarn --pure-lockfile and ./node_modules/.bin/bower install
Production build: grunt build, then NODE_ENV=production node dist/server/app.js (port 8080)
Or build locally: docker build . -t <name>, then docker run with GOOGLE_FONTS_API_KEY on port 8080
notable: Exports multiple font formats (eot, ttf, svg, woff, woff2) plus CSS snippets in one step
Public JSON API for listing fonts and getting per-font file URLs
Zip download endpoint with filters for subsets, formats, and variants
Final Docker image runs rootless on a minimal base with no dev dependencies
Prebuilt Docker images published via GitHub Packages
caveats: Requires a Google Fonts API key from Google before it will run
README says the project is largely on life-support, with much of its code and dependencies deprecated
The JSON API may be rate-limited
Client code is described as very legacy Angular
